main_text.l: ricordiæ,quæ præparavit ad gloriā. Ratio 2. Quia malus est, & natura filius iræ. Eph.2.3.

3. Cum in Deu respicit, & in eo acquiescit, optime habet. Huius sententiæ expositio extat Psal.123.2[?]. Ecce sicut oculi servorum ad manu dominorum fuorū,sicut oculi ancillæ ad manum dominę suę: ita oculi nostri ad Iehouā Deum nostrū, donec misereatur nostri.

4. Cum autem creaturas præ Creatore colit, maledictus est. Hier.17.5.Sic dicit Iehouah: Maledictus vir qui fidit homini, & ponit carnē brachium suum, & à Iehouah recedit cor eius. 6.Erit enim tanquam myrica in deserto, neq; videbit cū venerit bonum,&c.

5. Tribuitur autē conversioijs, qui jam antea à Deo aversi erant. Rom.5.10. Nam si,cum inimici essemus, reconciliati suimus Deo per morte filii eius, multo magis reconciliati servabimur per vitam ipsius. 1.Pet.2.25. Nam eratis velut oves errantes:sed conversi nunc estis ad pastore & curatorem animarum nostrarum.
6. Aversi à Deo infideles sunt & ἀντιλο-γικοί, Rom.10.21. Toto die expandi ma-nus

page.notes: Psal.123.2 is read as "123" with some doubt; the scan is faint. "Deu" is printed with a diacritic over the u that I could not resolve, so it is given as "Deu" with the mark not reproduced. Long s is written as plain s throughout. Printed u/v and i/j were normalised as the rules require (e.g., "uir" to "vir", "filij" to "filii"). "Iehouā" and the macron forms follow the scan.
